angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 4,730,760 km at 43.94 pc = 1.44 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 90185: the Hipparcos parallax (van Leeuwen 2007) the radius is computed with, 22.76 +/- 0.24 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1134/S1063773712050015): 43.937 +/- 0.463 pc; Gaia DR3 cannot see the star
radiusSource: Radius 6.8 +/- 0.29 solar radii from Computed here, not printed by a paper: 6.8 +/- 0.29 solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 1.44 +/- 0.06 mas of Hanbury Brown, Davis & Allen (1974), MNRAS 167, 121 (the Narrabri intensity interferometer; Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, Table 1, and the JMDC) and the Hipparcos parallax 22.76 +/- 0.24 mas (van Leeuwen 2007, XHIP) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/167.1.121): 4,730,760 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 9460 +/- 220 K from Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 169022: effective temperature 9460 +/- 220 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Code, Davis, Bless & Hanbury Brown (1976), ApJ 203, 417, HD 169022: effective temperature 9460 +/- 220 K (Table 6), from the measured angular diameter and the star's flux from the ultraviolet to the infrared (https://doi.org/10.1086/154093)
surfaceGravitySource: log g 3.57 from 1980A&AS...40..199P, measured from the star's Stroemgren photometry: SIMBAD's compilation holds no spectroscopic gravity of this star (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/1980A%26AS...40..199P)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps Sgr: spectral type B9IVp_lB? (1975ApJ...197..137S)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * eps Sgr: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * eps Sgr: projected rotation speed 236 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2005yCat.3244....0G)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
